title: USMCA and the Politics of Permanent Leverage
gist: Mexican analyst Brenda Estefan argues Washington's goal in the USMCA review is not to close a deal but to preserve permanent leverage over Mexico, which means the review is likely to stay deliberately open rather than conclude in 2027; the U.S. has split North America into two separate bilateral tracks, souring on Canada while keeping Mexico engaged, and is increasingly using cartel-corruption investigations rather than tariffs alone as its pressure instrument.

themes.theme: Leverage as the actual negotiating objective

insights.claim: The Trump administration's aim in the USMCA review is not to secure a specific set of concessions but to preserve the leverage that makes each subsequent concession easier to extract, which changes the entire logic of how the negotiation will unfold.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: If leverage rather than settlement is the goal, pricing a 'USMCA resolution' catalyst into Mexican assets is a mistake — the tail risk is indefinite open-endedness, not a clean deal.
insights.quote: The objective is not simply to secure concessions. It is to preserve the leverage that makes future concessions easier to extract.
insights.locator: So, what is the ultimate goal of the new Washington?

insights.claim: An administration that treats leverage as a strategic asset has little incentive to rush to a final USMCA deal, so consensus expectations that the review concludes in 2027 understate the probability of deliberate prolongation.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Contrarian to the 'review wraps next year' base case — position for a longer tail of trade uncertainty in Mexican industrial and auto-supply-chain names.
insights.quote: For an administration that treats leverage as a strategic asset, there is little incentive to rush toward a final and conclusive deal.
insights.locator: Some observers expect the USMCA review to conclude next year.

insights.claim: A comprehensive North American trade agreement may be timed for maximum political value late in Trump's term rather than early, implying deal announcement risk is back-loaded.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Suggests the trade-relief trade in Mexican equities and the peso is a later-cycle event; premature positioning bleeds carry.
insights.quote: If a comprehensive agreement is eventually reached, it may prove more politically valuable toward the end of President Trump’s term than at the beginning.
insights.locator: Keeping the review open preserves flexibility

insights.claim: Keeping the review open lets Washington link trade to an expanding agenda — organized crime, fentanyl trafficking, migration, Chinese companies free-riding on USMCA, water deliveries, energy policy and customs enforcement — so the trade file becomes a catch-all coercion vehicle.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Any Mexican policy dispute — water, energy regulation, Chinese FDI — can now transmit into trade risk; treat these as correlated rather than independent risk factors.
insights.quote: Keeping the review open preserves flexibility and allows the U.S. to connect trade negotiations to an expanding range of concerns
insights.locator: Keeping the review open preserves flexibility

insights.claim: The White House mindset toward Mexico was summarized to the author in Washington as "with Mexico if possible, without Mexico if necessary" — cooperation is preferred but never at the cost of surrendering leverage.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: A usable heuristic for handicapping U.S.-Mexico outcomes: Washington will accept a worse economic outcome rather than one that removes its optionality.
insights.quote: with Mexico if possible, without Mexico if necessary
insights.locator: One phrase I heard in Washington

insights.claim: The U.S. Trade Representative's framework treats North America as two distinct bilateral relationships — one arrangement with Canada, another with Mexico — rather than a single trilateral negotiation, effectively hollowing out USMCA's trilateral architecture.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Canada and Mexico risk premia should decouple; hedges that treat 'North American trade risk' as one factor will be mispriced.
insights.quote: Washington views North America not as a single trilateral negotiation but as two distinct bilateral relationships, each governed by different political calculations.

insights.claim: Within hours of the three North American leaders appearing together at the FIFA World Cup closing ceremony, Washington announced a new 50% tariff on a broad range of Canadian exports.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: A concrete 50% tariff shock on Canadian exports, delivered alongside a unity photo-op, is the clearest signal that diplomatic optics carry no predictive value for U.S. trade action.
insights.quote: The image was meant to project unity, yet within hours, Washington announced a new 50% tariff on a broad range of Canadian exports.
insights.locator: The image was meant to project unity

insights.claim: Canada is not participating in the trade talks of what is a de facto integrated North American market, while Mexico is still viewed by Washington as a partner worth engaging because progress is believed possible.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Relative-value implication: Mexico holds a better negotiating position than Canada despite weaker fundamentals — a case for CAD-underperformance versus MXN on trade-policy news.
insights.quote: The relationship with Canada has become noticeably sour. Mexico, by contrast, is still viewed as a partner worth engaging
insights.locator: The relationship with Canada has become noticeably sour.

insights.claim: A third round of bilateral U.S.-Mexico USMCA talks concluded in Mexico City with auto industry rules of origin and nondiscriminatory access to Mexico's electricity market still unresolved, and a new round scheduled for September in Washington.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Two named sticking points — auto rules of origin and power-market access — are the tradeable specifics; watch the September Washington round for movement on Mexican electricity liberalization.
insights.quote: contentious topics such as auto industry rules of origin and nondiscriminatory access to Mexico’s electricity market are still sticking points that will be discussed in a new round scheduled for September in Washington

insights.claim: The U.S. Trade Representative has said he hopes to present Trump and the other North American leaders with proposals by the end of the year, setting a near-term milestone in the review process.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: A stated year-end proposal deadline gives a discrete date to watch, though the author argues the framework matters more than the timeline.
insights.quote: U.S. Trade Representative Greer recently said he hopes to present President Trump and the other North American leaders with proposals by the end of the year.
insights.locator: U.S. Trade Representative Greer recently said

themes.theme: Judicial and anti-corruption channels as coercion

insights.claim: Investigations into alleged links between Mexican public officials and organized crime have become an independent instrument of U.S. leverage, distinct from and potentially more potent than tariffs, because they carry enormous political costs for Mexico's governing party.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Mexican political risk is now hostage to U.S. prosecutorial timing — a headline naming a senior official could move the peso independently of any trade development.
insights.quote: Because such probes carry enormous political costs for the governing party, they have become an especially powerful instrument of leverage in the broader bilateral relationship.
insights.locator: Trade is no longer the only channel

insights.claim: DEA Administrator Terry Cole framed the life sentence of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada as "only the beginning," pledging to pursue not just Mexican cartel leaders but the corrupt officials who enable them.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: An explicit U.S. pledge to prosecute Mexican officials is a forward-looking political-risk catalyst with no fixed calendar — an unhedgeable but recurring source of MXN volatility.
insights.quote: DEA Administrator Terry Cole declared that the conviction was “only the beginning,” pledging to continue pursuing not only Mexican cartel leaders but also the corrupt officials who enable them
insights.locator: Mexico, too, received its own reminder.

themes.theme: Structural asymmetry and Mexico's narrowing room

insights.claim: As long as access to the world's largest consumer market remains indispensable for Mexico, Washington retains extraordinary leverage well beyond trade itself — the asymmetry is structural, not cyclical or personality-driven.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Implies U.S. pressure on Mexico persists across administrations; do not model a post-Trump normalization of the bilateral bargaining balance.
insights.quote: As long as access to the world’s largest consumer market remains indispensable for Mexico, Washington will retain extraordinary leverage well beyond trade itself.
insights.locator: This ability to broaden the negotiating agenda

insights.claim: Three decades of integration have produced a manufacturing ecosystem in which intermediate goods cross the U.S.-Mexico border multiple times before becoming finished products, making rapid supply-chain substitution physically impossible regardless of political rhetoric.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Multi-crossing intermediate goods mean tariff incidence compounds; auto and electronics margins are more exposed to nominal tariff rates than headline numbers suggest.
insights.quote: Intermediate goods cross the border multiple times before becoming finished products. Supply chains and investment are deeply intertwined.

insights.claim: There is no realistic substitute for the U.S. market for Mexico in the foreseeable future, which means Mexican diversification rhetoric should be discounted as a negotiating posture rather than a credible alternative.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Discount Mexican announcements about pivoting to Europe or Asia; the binding constraint is geography and existing capital stock, not intent.
insights.quote: There is no realistic substitute for the U.S. market in the foreseeable future, and political rhetoric cannot alter that fact.

insights.claim: Not every U.S.-extracted concession harms Mexico — dismantling links between organized crime and public officials strengthens the Mexican state regardless of who demands it — but concessions that constrain Mexico's industrial, technological or regulatory autonomy deserve far greater scrutiny.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: A triage framework for reading each USMCA concession: security-and-corruption items are net positive for Mexican institutional quality; industrial-policy constraints are the ones that compress long-run competitiveness.
insights.quote: The challenge, therefore, is not to resist every concession, but to distinguish between those that strengthen Mexico and those that unnecessarily limit its future room for maneuver.
insights.locator: Other demands, by contrast, deserve far greater scrutiny.

insights.claim: After two decades of dealing with U.S. officials under both Republican and Democratic administrations, the author reports a qualitatively new sense of entitlement in Washington — an assumption that the U.S. sets terms and partners adjust, rather than allies pursuing common interests.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: A first-hand read that the shift is cultural and bipartisan-durable inside the U.S. system, not a Trump-specific tactic — raising the persistence of the new bargaining regime.
insights.quote: The language was less that of allies pursuing common interests than of a power convinced that its market and its geopolitical weight entitle it to define the rules.
insights.locator: During more than two decades of working with U.S. officials

insights.claim: North American diplomacy has inverted from decades of friction-reduction to a model where dialogue permanently coexists with pressure, with warm meetings between Sheinbaum and Greer carrying no signal about underlying negotiating trajectory.
insights.speaker: BRENDA ESTEFAN
insights.so_what: Discount positive diplomatic headlines as tradeable signal; only concrete tariff, rules-of-origin or enforcement actions carry information.
insights.quote: For decades, North American diplomacy sought to reduce friction among partners. Now, however, dialogue increasingly coexists with pressure.
